title: Scripture God-breathed; how to read (Philoc. 1 opening)
english: The anthology opens from Origen on the [[God-breathed >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:16]] character of the divine writings and how they are to be read and understood — including why obscurity and passages impossible or absurd at the mere letter are there, so that we seek the Spirit’s sense without despising what the letter rightly carries.

title: Scripture locked and sealed (Philoc. 2)
english: Scripture is [[locked and sealed >> Bible:Isaiah 29:11]]; the blesseds spoken in the singular and the plural must be weighed together, so that the reader does not treat the divine book as already open to every casual glance.

english: Origen counts the [[God-breathed >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:16]] books as twenty-two, matching the Hebrew letters, so that the church’s canon is taught as a closed, ordered library rather than an open heap.

title: Philoc. 27: Hardening of Pharaoh’s heart
english: Often [[the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart >> Bible:Exodus 9:12]] and [[I will harden Pharaoh’s heart >> Bible:Exodus 7:3]] unsettle almost every reader — unbelievers who call the saying unworthy of God, and believers who quarrel over it. Origen will not leave God as author of disobedience, nor invent a second god who hardens whom he wills by lot; the hardening must be read so that the Creator’s will is not made the cause of Pharaoh’s refusal.
